triage.note: Thirteen NUMBERED defects plus the R7 mislabel — numbered (14) in the fixture — reported as FIFTEEN failures, at an EXACT count. Nothing is DELETED in this fixture — both confidence sites render, all three helpers exist, the coverage strip exists and even carries a real percentage — because the demo defect was never a missing element. It was a present number with nothing beside it, and the coverage half's worse failure mode is a line that reads as reassurance. The original eleven: (1) the SIDE PANEL badge prints a bare `conf ${it.confidence ?? "—"}`, the 2026-08-24 demo verbatim; (2) the pane header carries `${docQual()}` but drops `${itemQual(it)}`, so a validator-flagged item reads like an untouched one; (3) `QUALIFIED` no longer lists `ambiguous`, so the one status meaning 'could not resolve this document' qualifies nothing and jpm-2024's column of 0.75s reads as plain numbers; (4) `docQual` reads a live control's current value instead of the RESPONSE's `doc_status` — the S8 read-at-request-time rule broken in the qualifier; (5) `itemQual` re-derives 'item-targeted' from the NUMBER (`it.confidence < 0.9`) instead of reading `score()`'s own `hits` list, a second definition in the display layer and a wrong one, since 0.85 is the ordinary base for an IBR item and 0.95 is what an untouched item scores — it flags clean items and stays silent on exactly the cvx-2015 shape; (6) `coverageStrip` reads `toc_manifest_mismatch`, which carries no coverage figure at all; (7) the 9.7-point understatement caveat is gone; (8) so is its reason, that interior gaps are not counted; (9) the line instead asserts the remainder is covered; (10) it performs the inverted arithmetic at all, `100 - outside` being pinned as forbidden on its own because the interior gaps were never in that subtraction; (11) and it labels the result an attributed share. PR #53 round 1 added two more: (12) R1 — `coverageStrip` is DEFINED, correct, and never CALLED, the banner assignment ending at the source ternary, which round 0's case could not see because it only ever read the function's body; (13) R3 — the badge class folds the document-level flag into the item-level one, so on jpm-2024 twenty-three identical amber badges cover one genuinely flagged item. WHY 13 NUMBERED DEFECTS BUT 15 FAILURES, stated because a count that does not match its list is the defect PR #46 R12 recorded — and PR #53 R9 caught the first version of this sentence getting it wrong twice over. The arithmetic: each of (1)-(13) produces exactly one failure, and the R7 mislabel, numbered (14) in the fixture, produces TWO — a missing `must_say` ('unattributed content:') and a forbidden `must_not_say` ('document coverage:'). 13 + 2 = 15. The earlier version led with whole-body pinning 'collapsing several defects into one failure', which explains none of the delta: (4), (5) and (6) each produced exactly one failure before that mechanism landed and one after, so the collapse changes the count by zero. (9), (10), (11) and the mislabel are pinned as FORBIDDEN wording rather than merely as missing wording, for the same reason `ui-exclusion-note-regression` pins 'the two panes match': a banner that overstates coverage, or labels non-coverage as coverage, is a failure of the task and not a shortcut. ONE `must_say` half is left INTACT — 'of the document lies outside every item', which the fixture still carries — so a check that blanket-failed the wording would overshoot by one. (Round 0 had two; the R7 rename moved 'document coverage:' out of `must_say` and into `must_not_say`, and this sentence was not updated until PR #53 R9 caught it.) The fixture yields three of four missing-`must_say` failures, and `min_conf_sites` is met exactly — both sites are present and both are wrong.
triage.ceiling: Same text-pin ceiling as ui-confidence-honesty, and the same warning against reading it as more: nothing here renders a badge, extracts a filing, or evaluates a template literal. Shape (5) is caught because the pinned body differs, not because anything measured that `it.confidence < 0.9` disagrees with `evidence.warnings` on a real fixture; shape (12) because the pinned assignment is absent, not because anything observed an empty banner. This fixture is also a poor instrument for asking whether ONE change would have been caught, since every shape's failures are mixed with the others — which is exactly how PR #53 R1/R2/R4 survived round 0. tasks/reviews/pr53_mutation_probe.py is the isolating counterpart: one defect per copy of the shipped file, ten of them, each asserted red, plus a control.
triage.red_first: Three states, all observed. (1) The real file went red first at 3cdfbf4 (main tip, index.html unmodified) with 9 failures, recorded verbatim in tasks/reviews/d7-red-first.txt — that run is what proves the check can see the demo defect. (2) This fixture then went red at 11/11 against the round-0 implementation, proving each shape is caught separately rather than as one blanket failure. (3) At PR #53 round 1 the count moved to 15/15 with shapes (12) and (13) added; the four new pins (call site, three whole bodies, the flag expression, the label) were each watched red BEFORE the repair against one-defect copies of the shipped file — tasks/reviews/pr53-r1-red.txt records all three attacks passing the round-0 check first, which is the finding, and pr53_mutation_probe.py re-runs them. Round 2 added no shape to this fixture; its count is unchanged at 15 because the two new pins (declaration count, banner assignment target) were already failing here through the shapes that existed.
